title: Compatibility layer and contributor checklist for primitive upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: define a repeatable, low-friction process for upgrading primitive design tokens and components (buttons, tables, charts) that preserves backwards compatibility and gives contributors a clear checklist. This ticket creates a compatibility layer pattern, contributor review checklist, codemod guidance, and communication templates for deprecation windows. Focus areas: token renames/aliases, semantic tokens vs raw values, runtime feature flags, docs banner/notice, and migration tooling.
acceptance_criteria: A compatibility wrapper pattern document exists with code examples for CSS-in-JS and compiled token bundles
Contributor checklist published in the repo that reviewers must sign off on
Two codemod examples (token rename, prop rename) are included in the scripts/upgrade-codemods folder
A 90/180 day deprecation schedule template and release note format available for PMs
Automated lint rule that warns on use of soon-to-be-deprecated token keys in storybook and unit tests
work_items: Draft compatibility-layer RFC with examples for aliasing tokens and fallback values
Define contributor review checklist and mandatory CI checks
Implement sample compatibility wrapper for Button and Table components
Create two codemods and integration tests
Add deprecation banners to affected Storybook stories and docs pages
Coordinate with eng to add token-lint rule and CI gating
Prepare communication templates for release notes, Slack, and internal changelog
risks: Large surface area: charts and tables touch many internal apps—risk of missed regressions
Codemods can’t cover custom token usage in user code; some manual follow-up expected
Maintainer burden if aliases are kept indefinitely; need a strict sunset timeline
Runtime performance concerns if compatibility wrappers run expensive lookups on hot paths
notes_and_decisions: Decision: use semantic token aliases (semantic.<purpose>) rather than direct raw value renames to minimize churn
Decision: default compatibility period is 180 days, with an optional extended window for enterprise customers
Trade-off: keep wrappers lightweight (O(1) lookup) and compile aliases into the build when possible
Follow-up: Engineering to provide a feature-flagged rollout for compatibility runtime toggle (ENG-45212)
Recommendation: pair any token removal with a migration codemod and a storybook PR that highlights changes
